llm_classification_pass.description: Phase 5: full-dataset LLM reclassification via classify_all.py, superseding the Phase 3 manual round trip that covered only the 3,554-row (12.2%) Uncategorized residual.
llm_classification_pass.method: Message Batches API, effort=high, structured JSON output

1_self_consistency.method: Independent second Batch API pass over 1,000 randomly sampled rows (seed 20260816), compared to the first pass.
1_self_consistency.finding: All 39 disagreements fell on first-pass medium (20) or low (19) confidence rows -- zero disagreements among high-confidence rows. Confidence is a reliable signal of the realistic accuracy ceiling.

2_agreement_with_reviewed_rows.method: Compared against data/recall_categories_llm_classified.csv, the 3,554-row manual Phase 3 pass over the original Uncategorized residual.
2_agreement_with_reviewed_rows.finding: Of the 436 raw disagreements: 41 are taxonomy expansions into labels that didn't exist in the old 18-label set (Eggs, Baby/Toddler Food, Pet Food/Treats); 116 are old-real-category rows the new pass moved to Uncategorized (111/116 low confidence -- reviewed by hand, these are bare/ambiguous descriptions the old manual pass over-guessed on, e.g. 'Nano Papa', 'Placenta', 'SOD'); 20 are old-Uncategorized rows the new pass resolved to a real category (improvement); 259 are true swaps among shared labels, explained by coverage rules added since the old pass (coffee creamer, formula, batter mix, cooked-bean dishes).

3_confidence_triage.method: Reviewed a stratified sample (10/category) of the 1,643 low-confidence rows outside Uncategorized, plus the full confidence breakdown by category.
3_confidence_triage.finding: No misclassifications found. Low confidence correctly flags genuinely thin or boundary-case descriptions (bare SKUs, novel/international products). Highest low-confidence shares match the doc's own Known Gaps: Baking Supplies 37.3%, Food Additives/Ingredients 26.8%, Beef/Pork/Poultry/Game Meats 23.7%.

4_category_coherence.method: 15 random product descriptions printed per category, all 21 categories (315 total), eyeballed for a category absorbing junk.
4_category_coherence.finding: All 21 categories coherent. No repeat of the 'clamshell -> Seafood' keyword-era bug class.

5_keyword_vs_llm_disagreement.method: Ran categories.py's assign_category() keyword rules against every description, compared to the LLM label per category (with Beef/Pork/Poultry/Eggs mapped onto the merged Beef/Pork/Poultry/Game Meats + Eggs labels).
5_keyword_vs_llm_disagreement.finding: Lowest agreement: Beef 18.5%, Pork 26.1%, Poultry/Eggs 37.5%, Grains/Cereal 39.2% -- exactly the failure classes categories.py's own docstring predicted (meat words read as flavoring/ingredient, not product, per FDA-vs-USDA jurisdiction). Highest agreement: Supplements 88.3%, Plant Protein 83.6%, Seafood 80.7%, Oils/Fats 78.0%.

6_residual_inspection.method: Read all 231 Uncategorized rows' full product descriptions.
6_residual_inspection.finding: Overwhelmingly bare SKUs/item codes, gift baskets and assortments, and unlabeled bulk shipments -- matches the taxonomy's own Uncategorized definition. Found one systematic miss: 13 rows matching the exact 'BATTER MIX X1, 50 LBS'-style bare-code pattern the Grains/Cereal rule's worked example explicitly covers. Patched directly to Grains/Cereal (confidence: high) in data/recall_categories_llm_full.csv. Residual after fix: 218 rows (0.75%).

step_3b_validation.verdict: All six checks pass. No systemic issues beyond the one fixed (13 rows). Step 4 (pipeline refactor) is cleared to proceed.
